sections.heading: Transform’s example
sections.content: Transform had a strong semantic-layer product and was vocal about solving difficult technical problems, putting pressure on dbt Labs, which was behind in bringing its own product to market. Yet Transform positioned itself as a friendly partner, hoping dbt’s community would be interested in its product. It had also done substantial work to make integration with dbt possible. When dbt acquired Transform, that prior integration work made post-acquisition integration easier.

sections.heading: The broader lesson
sections.content: Schottenstein described the approach as making a potential buyer notice the company by competing in an area where it had an advantage, but doing so in a friendly, open way. She cautioned against taking such a competitive stance that founders prematurely shut down conversations with an incumbent or potential buyer; keeping the relationship open preserves options.
